narrative:
The model estimated a 53.4% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is only slightly above a coin flip, but it was enough to cross the cutoff used for this decision, so your law school application was denied.

The most influential factor was your third-year class standing. You are in the first decile, while students who were accepted average around the sixth decile. This was the strongest signal and it pushed the prediction toward failure, so it weighed heavily against you. Your undergraduate GPA was the second most important factor, and it worked in your favor: at 3.40, it is above the accepted-student average of 3.23. Your upper-middle family income was the third most important factor and also pushed slightly toward passing; it is a common background among accepted students. Even so, those positive signals were not strong enough to offset the concern raised by your third-year standing.

To move forward, request a human review or appeal of the decision and provide any context that explains your third-year class rank. Ask an advisor about a concrete plan to strengthen your academic record, prepare for the bar exam, and consider whether retaking the LSAT or delaying reapplication would improve your case.
